not_covered: The United States moved to force TikTok's sale or ban it primarily due to national security concerns regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and the platform’s algorithm, which were subjects of CFIUS review [Source: ev-1].

Legislatively, President Biden signed the Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act on 2024-04-24, requiring ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by 90) or face a US ban [Source: ev-1].
The dispute was resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2025/06/10.[Source: ev-1]
This structure created a joint venture rather than an outright sale, giving Oracle about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations while ByteDance retained a majority interest [Source: ev-1].
SoftBank and other investors also participated in the investment [Source: ev-1].
